title: John Lennon, George Harrison and Ringo Starr attend Hollywood party | 1973
content:
John Lennon, Yoko Ono, George Harrison, and Ringo Starr attended a Hollywood party on 7 April 1973.

The event took place at the Beverly Hills home of Universal Studios VP Jennings Lang, and was a legal fundraiser and birthday party for Daniel Ellsberg, a political activist and former military analyst who had been charged with theft and conspiracy in what became known as the Pentagon Papers. Around 200 people attended, with entry costing $250 per couple.

The party was attended by a number of Hollywood luminaries, including Burt Lancaster, Barbra Streisand, Rod Steiger, Joni Mitchell, David Geffen, and Hugh Hefner.

Streisand performed several songs accompanied by Marvin Hamlisch on piano, and when a $3,000 bid for Lennon and Starr to play ‘With A Little Help From My Friends’ was submitted, she sang it instead.

Page last updated: 25 March 2026

Also on this day...

  • 2019: Ringo Starr and his All-Starr Band live: Tokyo Dome City Hall, Tokyo
  • 2009: The Beatles’ remastered CDs to be released on 09/09/09

  • 1971: Recording: Dear Boy, Uncle Albert/Admiral Halsey by Paul and Linda McCartney
  • 1970: Paul McCartney acquires the rights to Rupert The Bear
  • 1969: Mixing: Get Back, Don’t Let Me Down
  • 1967: Mixing: Sgt Pepper crossfades, With A Little Help From My Friends, Being For The Benefit Of Mr Kite!, Fixing A Hole, Lucy In The Sky With Diamonds
  • 1967: Paul McCartney films Jane Asher in Denver, and has the idea for Magical Mystery Tour
  • 1966: Recording: Tomorrow Never Knows, Got To Get You Into My Life
  • 1965: Filming: Help!
  • 1964: Filming: A Hard Day’s Night
  • 1963: The Beatles live: Savoy Ballroom, Southsea, Portsmouth
  • 1962: The Beatles live: Casbah Coffee Club, Liverpool
  • 1962: The Beatles live: Cavern Club, Liverpool (evening)
  • 1961: The Beatles live: Top Ten Club, Hamburg
